newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore share index follows U.S. markets higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore share index follows U.S. markets higher.

text.p: Singapore shares opened slightly firmer on Wednesday, following a fresh record closing high on Wall Street overnight.
By 0110 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials share index (STII) was 1.61 higher at 2,077.62 points.

Dealers said the opening move on the STII underestimated the firmness of the market because there had been a late blip on the index on Tuesday night, which pushed it up almost 20 points on relatively low volume.
"The market is mostly following New York on sentiment," said one dealer.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up 37.50 points overnight at 7,383.41.
Property group DBS Land resumed trading after announcing the purchase of 19.16 percent of healthcare and property group Parkway Holdings on Tuesday.
The stock rose to Singapore $4.88 (US$3.41), up four cents from its close on Monday, after brushing a high of S$4.92 at the open.
The biggest early gainer was computer card maker Creative Technology, which put on 80 cents, or three percent, to S$26.30.
